name: legal-retrieval-gold-v2
purpose: Deterministic retrieval evaluation against the supplied legal corpus (v1 plus paraphrased and wider-coverage cases)

ground_truth_policy.evidence_match: case expected_evidence must occur within a retrieved chunk; matching is case-insensitive after whitespace normalization
ground_truth_policy.section_metadata: authoritative provision identified from the supplied statute PDF
ground_truth_policy.status: gold-candidate; evidence verified verbatim against the indexed chunks (2026-10-01); freeze after source-text audit
ground_truth_policy.style: statutory: worded like the statute; paraphrase: plain-language question with little wording in common with the provision
ground_truth_policy.v2_changes: 7 v1 cases (evidence_fixed_in_v2) had expected evidence that occurs in no indexed chunk (curly quotes, PDF spacing artifacts, a spelling variant), so they could never pass; v2 quotes the indexed text. Section labels of hl-005, hl-008, hl-009 and hl-011 corrected. 31 cases added.

cases.query: What is the territorial extent of the Information Technology Act, 2000?
expected_evidence: It shall extend to the whole of India

cases.query: What does access mean under the Information Technology Act, 2000?
expected_evidence: gaining entry into, instructing or communicating with the logical, arithmetical, or memory function resources of a computer

cases.query: What makes an electronic signature reliable under the Information Technology Act?
expected_evidence: the signature creation data or the authentication data are, within the context in which they are used, linked to the signatory

cases.query: When does the Information Technology Act recognize information as satisfying a writing requirement in electronic form?
expected_evidence: rendered or made available in an electronic form

cases.query: When is a signature requirement satisfied by an electronic signature?
expected_evidence: authenticated by means of 1[electronic signature] affixed in such manner

cases.query: When is an electronic record dispatched under section 13?
expected_evidence: the dispatch of an electronic record occurs when it enters a computer resource outside the control of the originator

cases.query: When is an electronic record received if the addressee has designated a computer resource?
expected_evidence: receipt occurs at the time when the electronic record enters the designated computer resource

cases.query: When is an electronic record considered secure?
expected_evidence: deemed to be a secure electronic record from such point of time to the time of verification

cases.query: What conditions make an electronic signature a secure electronic signature?
expected_evidence: the signature creation data, at the time of affixing signature, was under the exclusive control of signatory

cases.query: What must a subscriber do to generate a key pair?
expected_evidence: corresponds to the private key of that subscriber which is to be listed in the Digital Signature Certificate

cases.query: When is a subscriber deemed to have accepted a Digital Signature Certificate?
expected_evidence: A subscriber shall be deemed to have accepted a Digital Signature Certificate if he publishes or authorises the publication

cases.query: What must a subscriber do if a private key has been compromised?
expected_evidence: the subscriber shall communicate the same without any delay to the Certifying Authority

cases.query: What conduct is covered by section 43 concerning unauthorized access?
expected_evidence: who is in charge of a computer, computer system or computer network

cases.query: When is publication of an electronic signature certificate prohibited?
expected_evidence: the certificate has been revoked or suspended

cases.query: When does the Information Technology Act apply to an offence committed outside India?
expected_evidence: the act or conduct constituting the offence or contravention involves a computer, computer system or computer network located in India

cases.query: What is a handloom under the Handlooms Act, 1985?
expected_evidence: means any loom, other than power loom

cases.query: When may the Central Government reserve an article for exclusive production by handlooms?
expected_evidence: after considering the recommendations made to it by the Advisory Committee

cases.query: Why is the Advisory Committee constituted under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: determining the nature of any article or class of articles that may be reserved for exclusive production by handlooms

cases.query: What factors must the Advisory Committee consider?
expected_evidence: the article or class of articles which is being produced traditionally by handlooms

cases.query: What is prohibited once an article has been reserved exclusively for handlooms?
expected_evidence: be produced by any loom, other than handloom

cases.query: What information or samples can the Central Government require from a manufacturer?
expected_evidence: require any manufacturer to furnish

cases.query: What powers does an authorised officer have to inspect a manufacturer's premises?
expected_evidence: may enter, at all reasonable times, any place or premises of any manufacturer

cases.query: When may an authorised officer search and seize under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: he may enter into and search such place or premises

cases.query: Which procedural law applies to searches and seizures under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: relating to searches and seizures shall, so far as may be, apply to every search or seizure made under this Act

cases.query: What is the penalty for producing articles in contravention of an order under section 3?
expected_evidence: punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months

cases.query: What constitutes a false statement under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: makes any statement or furnishes any information which is false in any material particular

cases.query: Are offences punishable under the Handlooms Act cognizable?
expected_evidence: every offence punishable under this Act shall be cognizable

cases.query: What protection does the Handlooms Act provide for actions taken in good faith?
expected_evidence: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Central Government, State Government or any officer or employee

cases.query: When can the Central Government exempt an article reserved for handlooms?
expected_evidence: the demand for any article or class of articles reserved by an order under section 3 outside India is such that it is not possible for the handloom industry to meet such demand

cases.query: Someone used my login password to pretend to be me online. What punishment can they face?
expected_evidence: make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person

cases.query: What is the punishment for impersonating someone over the internet to cheat them?
expected_evidence: cheats by personation

cases.query: Is it an offence to photograph someone's private parts and share the picture without consent?
expected_evidence: captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent

cases.query: What is the punishment for cyber terrorism?
expected_evidence: Whoever commits or conspires to commit cyber terrorism shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to imprisonment for life

cases.query: What happens to someone who posts lewd content online for the first time?
expected_evidence: shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years

cases.query: What is the penalty for publishing sexually explicit material in electronic form?
expected_evidence: material which contains sexually explicit act or conduct

cases.query: Can a company be made to pay compensation if it leaks customers' sensitive personal data because of weak security?
expected_evidence: is negligent in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices and procedures

cases.query: Up to what amount of claim can the adjudicating officer decide under the Information Technology Act?
expected_evidence: the claim for injury or damage does not exceed rupees five crore

cases.query: What is the penalty for misrepresentation to the Controller or a Certifying Authority?
expected_evidence: makes any misrepresentation to, or suppresses any material fact from the Controller or the Certifying Authority

cases.query: Can a service provider be punished for disclosing my personal information in breach of our contract?
expected_evidence: has secured access to any material containing personal information about another person

cases.query: Which offences under the Information Technology Act can be compounded?
expected_evidence: may compound offences, other than offences for which the punishment for life or imprisonment for a term exceeding three years has been provided

cases.query: Will I get bail for an IT Act offence that carries three years in jail?
expected_evidence: the offence punishable with imprisonment of three years shall be bailable

cases.query: Which police officer can investigate a cyber crime under the IT Act?
expected_evidence: shall investigate any offence under this Act

cases.query: Is a website platform responsible for illegal content uploaded by its users?
expected_evidence: an intermediary shall not be liable for any third party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by him

cases.query: When does an intermediary lose its exemption from liability?
expected_evidence: fails to expeditiously remove or disable access to that material

cases.query: Can the police arrest someone in a hotel without a warrant for a suspected cyber offence?
expected_evidence: may enter any public place and search and arrest without warrant any person found therein

cases.query: Does the Information Technology Act override other laws?
expected_evidence: shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law

cases.query: If a company breaks the IT Act, can its managers be held personally liable?
expected_evidence: was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of business of the company

cases.query: Who gives expert opinion on electronic evidence before a court under the Information Technology Act?
expected_evidence: providing expert opinion on electronic form evidence

cases.query: Is it a crime to knowingly keep a stolen phone?
expected_evidence: dishonestly receive or retains any stolen computer resource or communication device

cases.query: How long can a powerloom owner keep making an item after it is reserved for handlooms?
expected_evidence: may continue to be so engaged till the expiry of three months from the date of such reservation

cases.query: What is a power loom under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: a loom which is worked by power

cases.query: Does a business that only dyes or prints cloth count as a processor under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: engaged in any ancillary process subsequent to the production of cloth, such as dyeing, bleaching

cases.query: When must a seized powerloom be given back to its owner?
expected_evidence: no prosecution has been launched within six months of such seizure, it shall be returned

cases.query: What happens to articles produced in contravention of a reservation order under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: shall be forfeited to the Central Government

cases.query: What happens if a manufacturer refuses to show its account books to the authorised officer?
expected_evidence: fails to produce, or damages or destroys any such books

cases.query: Is attempting or abetting a contravention of a handloom reservation order an offence?
expected_evidence: attempts to contravene or abets the contravention of any order made under section 3 shall be deemed to have contravened that order

cases.query: Is a cooperative society treated as a company for offences under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: deemed to be registered under any law for the time being in force, a firm or other association of individuals

cases.query: Which powers of the Central Government cannot be delegated under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: other than the power to make orders under section 3 or under section 18 or to make rules under section 19

cases.query: Can powerlooms make reserved handloom items if they are only for export?
expected_evidence: solely for the purposes of export or for research

cases.query: Does the Handlooms (Reservation of Articles for Production) Act apply to the whole of India?
expected_evidence: It extends to the whole of India
